question: Padma Bhushan Kumari Kamala is associated with which Indian dance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kumari Kamala** was an exceptional Indian classical **Kathak dancer **who was born on June 16th, 1934.

 
 
• She made appearances in over 100 Tamil, Kannada, Telegu, and Hindi films as a kid dancer.
 
• With the **aid of Shankar Rao Vyas**, she became well-versed in Hindustani classical music, and **Lachhu Maharaj in Bombay trained her in Kathak.**
 
• With **"Nam Iruvar," her film**, she achieved great success.
 
• She starred in the **lead role of "Jagathalaprathapan," a Tamil film**.
 
• She was asked to play for Queen Elizabeth II's coronation celebrations in 1953, and during the 1950s, she went on tour through China and Japan.
 
• Even after receiving the **Branta Professorship in 1975**, she attended Colgate University for two terms.
 
• In **1970**, she received the **Padma Bhushan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kathak:

 
 
• The well-known ancient Indian classical dance known as Kathak is said to have originated with the nomadic storytellers from North India known as Kathakars.
 
• These Kathakars traveled and told tales using songs, dances, and music that were reminiscent of classical Greek theatre.
 
• The foundations of Kathak are rooted in the Natya Shastra, an ancient Sanskrit text written by Bharata Muni.
 
• The three chief sections of a Kathak dance are:
 
 
• Invocation: The act of an artist offering a prayer or salutation to God and their guru is known as an invocation.
 
 
• Hindu performers employ mudras, or hand gestures, to convey the same message.
 
• On Muslim holidays, the artist presents a "salami."
 
 
 
• Nritta: The artist's portrayal of pure dancing.
 
 
• He or she begins by moving the neck, wrists, and eyebrows slowly and elegantly.
 
• The quick sequences according to "bols" come next. A bol is a brief rhythmic pattern sequence. Here, the artist also demonstrates lively footwork.
 
 
 
• Nritya: In this piece, the performer uses facial expressions, slow body motions, and vocal and instrumental music to tell a tale or explore a theme.
